The Challenge

As the Senior Manager of the Cyber Threat Research & Intelligence team, you will guide Adobe's efforts to predict, identify, and respond to the changing threat environment. Your position is key to delivering high-quality intelligence at tactical, operational, and strategic levels. This intelligence helps Adobe's security teams and executive leaders make informed, proactive decisions. You will develop and enhance a leading threat research and intelligence program that transforms raw threat data into actionable insights. This program supports defenses based on adversary behavior and keeps Adobe ahead of advanced threat actors.

This is an opportunity to lead with purpose, build Adobe's intelligence strategy, and make a measurable impact on how the organization understands and responds to important threats.

What You Will Do

  • Develop and take responsibility for the strategic vision of Adobe's Cyber Threat Research & Intelligence program, covering tactical, operational, and strategic intelligence pillars.
  • Lead a senior team of threat intelligence researchers, balancing deep technical research with timely intelligence production and collaborator engagement.
  • Coordinate the full intelligence lifecycle — from collection and processing to analysis, production, and dissemination — ensuring intelligence outputs are relevant, accurate, timely, and actionable.
  • Build and manage Adobe's threat actor tracking program, maintaining profiles on advanced persistent threat (APT) groups, cyber criminal organizations, and hacktivists relevant to Adobe's industry and attack surface.
  • Produce and deliver intelligence products at multiple levels: tactical reports (IOCs, TTPs, YARA/Sigma rules), operational assessments (campaign analysis, actor attribution), and strategic briefings (threat landscape, industry trends, geopolitical risk).
  • Partner closely with Cyber Threat Hunt, CSIRT, Detection Engineering, and Red Team to ensure intelligence directly informs defensive operations, detection development, and incident response.
  • Drive Adobe's engagement with external intelligence communities, ISACs, government partners, and commercial threat intelligence providers to improve collection coverage and sharing.
  • Build a high-performing team through coaching, career development, and technical mentorship, while encouraging a collaborative and inclusive environment that promotes intellectual rigor and continuous learning!
  • Regularly brief senior leadership and key collaborators on the threat landscape, emerging risks, and intelligence program outcomes.

What You Need to Succeed

  • 8+ years in cybersecurity, with experience leading threat intelligence or threat research functions.
  • Deep expertise across the intelligence lifecycle, including collection management, all-source analysis, and structured analytic techniques (ACH, Kill Chain, Diamond Model, MITRE ATT&CK).
  • Established background in developing and presenting tactical, operational, and strategic intelligence reports to technical and executive viewers.
  • Strong understanding of threat actor ecosystems — including nation-state groups, eCrime actors, and insider threats — and the tradecraft used to track and attribute them.
  • Experience operationalizing threat intelligence through SIEM, SOAR, and TIP integrations, and converting intelligence into detection logic and defensive controls.
  • Familiarity with a broad range of collection sources including OSINT, dark web monitoring, malware analysis outputs, and commercial intelligence feeds.
  • Demonstrated success in building partnerships across security, engineering, legal, and business teams, and with external government and industry partners.
  • Ability to distill complex threat analysis into clear, compelling narratives that drive executive decision-making and security investment.
  • Experience building or maturing cybersecurity programs, including intelligence requirements processes, metrics frameworks, and team operating models.

The Opportunity Your mandate is to find security problems that don't scale and engineer them away. As a Senior Security Automation Engineer, you will build automation and AI-assisted frameworks to scale Adobe's web application protection across a diverse edge-security environment. You will pinpoint critical security workflows that remain manual, fragmented, or tough to scale. Afterward, you will re-engineer these into reliable systems, including vulnerability response, WAF policy validation, coverage assessment, multi-vendor automation, and enabling product teams to serve themselves. This is a build role for a senior engineer who combines strong software engineering skills and security judgment . You will help identify where AI can significantly improve security engineering. You will build systems and evaluation frameworks needed to use AI safely. You will also turn security expertise into capabilities that scale across Adobe. What you'll Do Develop production-ready automation and AI-supported systems for web and edge security processes across various WAF/CDN platforms. Recognize repetitive or high-friction security processes and transform them into scalable services, APIs, pipelines, and self-service options for product teams. Develop vulnerability-response automation, incorporating AI-assisted analysis and WAF rule creation — alongside validation, evaluation, regression testing, and secure deployment. Build automation around vulnerability intelligence, control coverage, policy lifecycle, configuration drift, and measurement of control effectiveness. Develop abstractions and integrations that reduce the operational complexity of supporting multiple WAF vendors. Build evaluation frameworks for AI-assisted security workflows and outputs — measuring correctness, consistency, behavioral drift, false-positive and false-negative rates, and readiness for production use. Partner with security architects and product teams to translate security requirements into reusable engineering capabilities. Raise the engineering bar through architecture, testing, CI/CD, observability, documentation, and mentoring. Proactively identify where AI and automation can meaningfully improve the team's effectiveness — and where human security judgment should stay in the loop. What you need to succeed 6+ years in software engineering, security engineering, or security automation, with production code you've shipped, not just vendor tooling you've configured. Strong proficiency in Python, TypeScript, or a comparable language, with experience building production-quality services and automation. Proven experience designing, building, and operating production services, APIs, or automation systems at scale, including observability, reliability measurement, controlled rollout and rollback, and ownership of production failures. Strong systems-design judgment, the ability to decide when to build abstractions, when to integrate existing platforms, and when automation would add complexity rather than remove it. Solid fundamentals in web, application, and edge security – you understand how web applications face threats and protections, and can apply that knowledge to engineering choices. Experience developing AI/LLM-assisted systems, or demonstrated ability to apply contemporary AI engineering approaches, structured outputs, evaluation, regression testing, and human-in-the-loop controls, to production workflows. Ability to work independently on unstructured problems and make defensible, risk-based decisions. Strong written and verbal communication; you can detail system logic and explain technical decisions, risks, and tradeoffs to engineers and non-technical collaborators. Preferred Deep production experience with LLM-integrated or agentic systems, including agent orchestration, prompt/context engineering, or autonomous multi-step workflows. Deep understanding of HTTP parsing, normalization, and protocol edge cases — including encoding discrepancies, request smuggling, and header ambiguity — and how they affect WAF efficacy and false-positive/false-negative behavior. Experience with vulnerability intelligence data (EPSS, CISA KEV, CVSS) and how it should -and shouldn't - drive prioritization. Experience building self-service security capabilities or platform tooling adopted by other teams. full_job_description_raw:
The Opportunity

Your mandate is to find security problems that don't scale and engineer them away.

As a Senior Security Automation Engineer, you will build automation and AI-assisted frameworks to scale Adobe's web application protection across a diverse edge-security environment. You will pinpoint critical security workflows that remain manual, fragmented, or tough to scale. Afterward, you will re-engineer these into reliable systems, including vulnerability response, WAF policy validation, coverage assessment, multi-vendor automation, and enabling product teams to serve themselves.

This is a build role for a senior engineer who combines strong software engineering skills and security judgment. You will help identify where AI can significantly improve security engineering. You will build systems and evaluation frameworks needed to use AI safely. You will also turn security expertise into capabilities that scale across Adobe.

What you'll Do

  • Develop production-ready automation and AI-supported systems for web and edge security processes across various WAF/CDN platforms.
  • Recognize repetitive or high-friction security processes and transform them into scalable services, APIs, pipelines, and self-service options for product teams.
  • Develop vulnerability-response automation, incorporating AI-assisted analysis and WAF rule creation — alongside validation, evaluation, regression testing, and secure deployment.
  • Build automation around vulnerability intelligence, control coverage, policy lifecycle, configuration drift, and measurement of control effectiveness.
  • Develop abstractions and integrations that reduce the operational complexity of supporting multiple WAF vendors.
  • Build evaluation frameworks for AI-assisted security workflows and outputs — measuring correctness, consistency, behavioral drift, false-positive and false-negative rates, and readiness for production use.
  • Partner with security architects and product teams to translate security requirements into reusable engineering capabilities.
  • Raise the engineering bar through architecture, testing, CI/CD, observability, documentation, and mentoring.
  • Proactively identify where AI and automation can meaningfully improve the team's effectiveness — and where human security judgment should stay in the loop.

What you need to succeed

  • 6+ years in software engineering, security engineering, or security automation, with production code you've shipped, not just vendor tooling you've configured.
  • Strong proficiency in Python, TypeScript, or a comparable language, with experience building production-quality services and automation.
  • Proven experience designing, building, and operating production services, APIs, or automation systems at scale, including observability, reliability measurement, controlled rollout and rollback, and ownership of production failures.
  • Strong systems-design judgment, the ability to decide when to build abstractions, when to integrate existing platforms, and when automation would add complexity rather than remove it.
  • Solid fundamentals in web, application, and edge security – you understand how web applications face threats and protections, and can apply that knowledge to engineering choices.
  • Experience developing AI/LLM-assisted systems, or demonstrated ability to apply contemporary AI engineering approaches, structured outputs, evaluation, regression testing, and human-in-the-loop controls, to production workflows.
  • Ability to work independently on unstructured problems and make defensible, risk-based decisions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; you can detail system logic and explain technical decisions, risks, and tradeoffs to engineers and non-technical collaborators.

Preferred

  • Deep production experience with LLM-integrated or agentic systems, including agent orchestration, prompt/context engineering, or autonomous multi-step workflows.
  • Hands-on experience with one or more major WAF/CDN technologies, such as AWS WAF, Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, or Mod Security/CRS, at a configuration or rule-authoring level.
  • Deep understanding of HTTP parsing, normalization, and protocol edge cases — including encoding discrepancies, request smuggling, and header ambiguity — and how they affect WAF efficacy and false-positive/false-negative behavior.
  • Experience with vulnerability intelligence data (EPSS, CISA KEV, CVSS) and how it should -and shouldn't - drive prioritization.
  • Experience building self-service security capabilities or platform tooling adopted by other teams.

You think in systems and build reusable, maintainable component libraries — with tokens, variables, and accessibility baked in — that let the whole team ship faster. You move fast, prototyping ideas in hours rather than days to validate concepts before full build. You’re excited about AI and want to help define new interaction paradigms. trategy and product sense: you connect design craft to measurable business and customer impact, reason in assertions, evidence, and trade-offs, and frame problems before jumping to solutions. A collaborative, people-first leadership style — coaching designers and engineers, influencing senior partners with clear narratives, and creating shared ownership of outcomes. Nice to have: experience with developer tools or technical products, native or cross-platform UI (e.g., Electron), and an understanding of code editors and IDEs. About the Role

Adobe is seeking a passionate engineer to join the Adobe Genuine Engineering team. This group protects Adobe's ecosystem from fraud, abuse, and misuse using intelligent systems worldwide.

In this role, you will compose and develop our unified graph along with the detection systems running on it. You will merge multiple isolated fraud graphs into one scalable source that identifies non-genuine and abusive signals across hundreds of millions of users. You will manage the entire lifecycle: starting from raw behavioral and account data, progressing through large-scale graph modeling and ingestion using Databricks and Spark, applying Graph Data Science algorithms and graph ML, and delivering production-ready detection for enforcement.

This role is for an engineer eager to manage graph systems entirely, covering schema, pipelines, community detection, and graph ML rather than using pre-built solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and evolve a unified graph schema that merges multiple fraud and account data sources into one consistent, rebuildable model.
  • Develop and enhance large-scale graph ingestion and feature pipelines on Databricks and Spark, converting raw behavioral and account events into refined graph nodes, edges, and properties.
  • Apply Graph Data Science (GDS) algorithms including community detection (WCC, Louvain, Label Propagation), centrality (PageRank), and node embeddings (FastRP, Node2Vec) to identify abuse rings, shared-entity clusters, and coordinated fraud.
  • Develop graph machine learning models, including Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), to extract high-value risk signals from network structure, and incorporate them into downstream ML workflows.
  • Translate prototypes into production graph systems that are scalable, reliable, and observable, and drive query and inference performance through modeling and serving-side optimization.
  • Own operational health of the graph platform: incremental refresh, supernode handling, monitoring, and cost efficiency at scale.
  • Contribute to MLOps and data-engineering practices: pipeline orchestration, versioning, CI/CD, automated retraining, and production monitoring.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with data science, product, and platform teams; experimentation rigor, and responsible AI.
  • Stay current with advances in graph ML and network science and bring relevant innovations into Adobe's products.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or graduate degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or related field.
  • 6+ years of professional experience building and deploying data or ML solutions at scale.
  • Solid programming skills in Python, with practical experience developing extensive data pipelines on Databricks and Spark.
  • Practical experience working with graph platforms such as Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, TigerGraph, or Memgraph, along with applying the Graph Data Science (GDS) library.
  • Practical experience implementing GDS algorithms like PageRank, Louvain/Label Propagation for community detection, or Node Embeddings (FastRP, Node2Vec) to extract insights from network data.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of the entire data and ML lifecycle, covering ingestion, feature engineering, deployment, and monitoring.
  • Strong grasp of data modeling, query optimization, and production system integration.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in applying Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and connecting GDS pipelines with downstream machine learning workflows.
  • Experience in fraud detection, anomaly detection, or behavioral modeling.
  • Familiarity with Neo4j Aura or other managed graph databases, and with large-scale incremental graph refresh and supernode management.

Data-Informed Decision Making & Strategic Business Partnership Act as a strategic Finance partner to Marketing leadership, connecting business strategy, marketing priorities, and financial outcomes. This Marketing Finance Lead position is a strategic finance leader supporting the Global Marketing Organization, focused on providing thought leadership across planning and investment decisions. 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

1. Data-Informed Decision Making & Strategic Business Partnership 

  • Act as a strategic Finance partner to Marketing leadership, connecting business strategy, marketing priorities, and financial outcomes. 

  • Build partnerships across Marketing and Finance to drive alignment, accountability, and effective decision-making. 

  • Partner with leaders to evaluate investment priorities, resource allocation, and trade-offs, ensuring spending aligns with strategic objectives. 

 

2. Marketing Effectiveness & Investment Optimization 

  • Develop financial analyses and scenarios that translate business questions into clear implications, recommendations, and actions. 

  • Develop a Finance point of view on investment priorities, trade-offs, risks, and opportunities and influence decisions through clear recommendations. 

  • Partner with Marketing teams to evaluate marketing performance, improve returns, and recommend where investments can be optimized. 

  • Create executive business reviews and presentations that translate financial and marketing trends into clear business implications and recommended actions, including end-to-end story development and executive-ready visualization. 
     

3. Budget Management & Financial Planning 

  • Lead financial planning and budget management, including forecasting, close, variance analysis, risks and opportunities, and scenario planning. 

  • Synthesize financial and business trends into concise narratives that clearly communicate what happened, why it matters, and what should happen next. 

  • Use AI, process automation, and data capabilities to improve FP&A and analytical workflows, accelerate insights, and enable better decision-making. 
     

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE 

  • 7+ years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, financial analytics, or related roles. 

  • Experience with financial modeling, forecasting, budgeting, and scenario analysis, capable of converting data into strategic recommendations. 

  • Strong executive communication expertise, demonstrated by independently developing leadership presentations and turning complex analysis into clear, compelling narratives. 

  • Ability to build effective partnerships, influence senior leaders, and navigate complex cross-functional decisions. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of distilling complex information into clear messages for executive audiences. 

  • Creative and structured approach to problem-solving, capable of working effectively through ambiguity. 

  • Experience applying AI tools to improve productivity, analysis, or workflows, with the ability to identify and champion new ways AI can improve Finance processes and decision-making. 

  • Experience with data visualization, reporting, or automation tools such as Power BI or Power Automate is a plus; familiarity with SQL is preferred.

full_job_description_raw:
Adobe is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join the Adobe Risk Platform (ARP) team. ARP is Adobe's centralized, adaptive system for detecting, preventing, and mitigating fraud and abuse across products and services — protecting surfaces like Commerce, Stock, and Firefly with real-time risk decisions, without degrading the customer experience.

In this position, you will help build and develop machine learning models to identify fraudulent activity, detect abusive account behavior, and protect the experience of hundreds of millions of users. You'll work across the model lifecycle from raw behavioral data and feature engineering, to model training, deployment, and monitoring alongside senior engineers on the team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Help build and train ML models covering various fraud and abuse areas. These include financial transaction fraud, device-related deception, and account and identity abuse. The goal is a unified, continuously-updated trust and risk score.
  • Contribute to feature engineering across transaction, device, and behavioral event data.
  • Build and maintain feature pipelines on Databricks and Spark, transforming raw transaction and device event data into high-quality model inputs.
  • Help translate prototypes into production ML systems, working with senior engineers on scalability, reliability, and observability.
  • Support MLOps practices: experiment tracking, model versioning, CI/CD, and production monitoring.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with data science, product, and platform teams to understand fraud and abuse patterns across Adobe's surfaces.
  • Stay ahead of advances in ML/AI, particularly in fraud detection and behavioral modeling, and bring relevant ideas to the team.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 3+ years of professional experience building and deploying ML solutions, or equivalent experience through internships, research, or personal projects.
  • Solid programming skills in Python, with hands-on experience in PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, or similar frameworks.
  • Working understanding of the ML lifecycle — from data collection through deployment and monitoring.
  • Eagerness to learn model optimization, inference efficiency, and production system integration, with support from senior engineers on the team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Coursework, projects, or professional experience in any of: payment fraud, device fingerprinting, account takeover detection, anomaly detection, or graph-based modeling.
  • Exposure to sequence modeling, transformer architectures, or graph neural networks.
  • Familiarity with Databricks, Spark, or large-scale transactional/event pipelines.

full_job_description_raw:
Adobe is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join the Adobe Risk Platform (ARP) team. ARP is Adobe's centralized, adaptive system for detecting, preventing, and mitigating fraud and abuse across products and services — protecting surfaces like Commerce, Stock, and Firefly with real-time risk decisions, without degrading the customer experience.

In this position, you will help build and develop machine learning models to identify fraudulent activity, detect abusive account behavior, and protect the experience of hundreds of millions of users. You'll work across the model lifecycle from raw behavioral data and feature engineering, to model training, deployment, and monitoring alongside senior engineers on the team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Help build and train ML models covering various fraud and abuse areas. These include financial transaction fraud, device-related deception, and account and identity abuse. The goal is a unified, continuously-updated trust and risk score.
  • Contribute to feature engineering across transaction, device, and behavioral event data.
  • Build and maintain feature pipelines on Databricks and Spark, transforming raw transaction and device event data into high-quality model inputs.
  • Help translate prototypes into production ML systems, working with senior engineers on scalability, reliability, and observability.
  • Support MLOps practices: experiment tracking, model versioning, CI/CD, and production monitoring.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with data science, product, and platform teams to understand fraud and abuse patterns across Adobe's surfaces.
  • Stay ahead of advances in ML/AI, particularly in fraud detection and behavioral modeling, and bring relevant ideas to the team.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 5+ years of professional experience building and deploying ML solutions, or equivalent experience through internships, research, or personal projects.
  • Solid programming skills in Python, with hands-on experience in PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, or similar frameworks.
  • Working understanding of the ML lifecycle — from data collection through deployment and monitoring.
  • Eagerness to learn model optimization, inference efficiency, and production system integration, with support from senior engineers on the team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Coursework, projects, or professional experience in any of: payment fraud, device fingerprinting, account takeover detection, anomaly detection, or graph-based modeling.
  • Exposure to sequence modeling, transformer architectures, or graph neural networks.
  • Familiarity with Databricks, Spark, or large-scale transactional/event pipelines.

description:
Builds and leads Adobe’s Adversarial Fraud Testing function within Global Consumer Trust. Proactively simulates and recreates real-world fraud and abuse attacks against Adobe’s externally facing products and fraud controls to identify weaknesses and validate defenses. Partners across Fraud Prevention, Product, Engineering, Security, and other organizations to translate adversarial findings into stronger controls, product improvements, and systemic risk reduction. Establishes repeatable testing methodologies and ensures remediation is validated through ongoing adversarial testing. What you’ll do Build and lead Adobe’s Adversarial Fraud Testing function within Global Consumer Trust, proactively testing how fraudsters and other bad actors may exploit Adobe’s products, services, and fraud controls. Develop an adversarial testing strategy and methodology that safely simulates real-world fraud and abuse across customer journeys, APIs, account creation, payments, entitlements, and other externally facing product experiences. Lead the recreation of significant fraud attacks to understand how controls were bypassed, identify weaknesses, and determine opportunities to strengthen Adobe’s defenses. Partner with Fraud Prevention, Product, Engineering, Security, and other teams to design adversarial tests, evaluate controls, and prioritize remediation of identified gaps. Build repeatable testing capabilities using automation, APIs, scripting, and other technical approaches to simulate fraud and abuse at scale. Validate new and existing fraud controls by testing whether mitigations effectively disrupt attack paths and reduce opportunities for circumvention. Establish clear processes for documenting findings, assessing risk, communicating recommendations, and tracking remediation through completion and retesting. Identify patterns across adversarial tests and real-world incidents to surface systemic weaknesses and influence Adobe’s fraud prevention strategy and product roadmaps. Build and develop a high-performing team with the technical, fraud, and adversarial expertise needed to anticipate and reproduce evolving attack techniques. What you need to succeed Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Economics, or a related field, plus 10+ years of hands-on industry experience. Demonstrated experience leading technical teams in fraud prevention, adversarial testing, security, abuse prevention, risk engineering, or a related field. Strong understanding of how fraudsters and other bad actors exploit digital products, customer journeys, APIs, identity systems, payments, and business processes. Technical fluency with APIs, automation, scripting, data analysis, and modern web and cloud architectures, with the ability to effectively lead highly technical testing. Must have: Python/similar programming, APIs/HTTP, automation, debugging, Git, data/SQL, ability to understand product architecture. Useful: JavaScript, cloud services, browser automation, authentication/identity systems, CI/CD, security testing tools. Strong adversarial mindset with the ability to think creatively about how controls and intended product behaviors could be circumvented or abused. Experience developing structured testing methodologies and translating findings into actionable product, engineering, and fraud-control improvements. Proven ability to influence Product, Engineering, Fraud, Security, and senior leaders without direct authority. Builds and leads Adobe’s Adversarial Fraud Testing function within Global Consumer Trust. Proactively simulates and recreates real-world fraud and abuse attacks against Adobe’s externally facing products and fraud controls to identify weaknesses and validate defenses. 

Partners across Fraud Prevention, Product, Engineering, Security, and other organizations to translate adversarial findings into stronger controls, product improvements, and systemic risk reduction. Establishes repeatable testing methodologies and ensures remediation is validated through ongoing adversarial testing. 

What you’ll do 

  • Build and lead Adobe’s Adversarial Fraud Testing function within Global Consumer Trust, proactively testing how fraudsters and other bad actors may exploit Adobe’s products, services, and fraud controls. 

  • Develop an adversarial testing strategy and methodology that safely simulates real-world fraud and abuse across customer journeys, APIs, account creation, payments, entitlements, and other externally facing product experiences. 

  • Lead the recreation of significant fraud attacks to understand how controls were bypassed, identify weaknesses, and determine opportunities to strengthen Adobe’s defenses. 

  • Partner with Fraud Prevention, Product, Engineering, Security, and other teams to design adversarial tests, evaluate controls, and prioritize remediation of identified gaps. 

  • Build repeatable testing capabilities using automation, APIs, scripting, and other technical approaches to simulate fraud and abuse at scale. 

  • Validate new and existing fraud controls by testing whether mitigations effectively disrupt attack paths and reduce opportunities for circumvention. 

  • Establish clear processes for documenting findings, assessing risk, communicating recommendations, and tracking remediation through completion and retesting. 

  • Identify patterns across adversarial tests and real-world incidents to surface systemic weaknesses and influence Adobe’s fraud prevention strategy and product roadmaps. 

  • Build and develop a high-performing team with the technical, fraud, and adversarial expertise needed to anticipate and reproduce evolving attack techniques. 

What you need to succeed 

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Economics, or a related field, plus 10+ years of hands-on industry experience.

  • Demonstrated experience leading technical teams in fraud prevention, adversarial testing, security, abuse prevention, risk engineering, or a related field. 

  • Strong understanding of how fraudsters and other bad actors exploit digital products, customer journeys, APIs, identity systems, payments, and business processes. 

  • Technical fluency with APIs, automation, scripting, data analysis, and modern web and cloud architectures, with the ability to effectively lead highly technical testing. 

  • Must have: Python/similar programming, APIs/HTTP, automation, debugging, Git, data/SQL, ability to understand product architecture. 

  • Useful: JavaScript, cloud services, browser automation, authentication/identity systems, CI/CD, security testing tools. 

  • Strong adversarial mindset with the ability to think creatively about how controls and intended product behaviors could be circumvented or abused. 

  • Experience developing structured testing methodologies and translating findings into actionable product, engineering, and fraud-control improvements. 

  • Proven ability to influence Product, Engineering, Fraud, Security, and senior leaders without direct authority. 

  • Strong judgment and ability to balance effective adversarial testing with customer, business, security, legal, and operational considerations. 

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex attack paths and technical findings into clear business risks and executive recommendations.

You will own hands-on buildout of the agent across the full stack and across Adobe's target platforms, from desktop and mobile to web and embedded surfaces. Enthusiasm for pushing the boundary of what AI-augmented engineering can look like at the frontier. Full-stack engineering depth sufficient to contribute across the agent's entire surface area — including backend services, client SDKs, and platform-specific integration patterns for Adobe's target platforms. Strong engineering craft: readable, well-structured, production-quality code; opinionated views on testing, local dev ergonomics, and the scaffolding that helps a team stay productive as a codebase grows. Clear communication skills — able to discuss technical tradeoffs with PM leads and senior technical stakeholders, flag issues early, and collaborate effectively across disciplines. Comfort operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where the underlying models, frameworks, and user expectations are all rapidly evolving — strong enough foundations to move fast without building on sand. Experience collaborating cross-functionally with product, design, platform, and security teams in the context of shipping user-facing AI products. Senior Multidisciplinary Designer  

Adobe Creative

 

Our Company 

Empowering everyone to create. 

Adobe empowers everyone, everywhere to imagine, create and bring digital experiences to life. From creators and students to small businesses, global enterprises and nonprofit organizations, customers choose Adobe products to create, collaborate, grow, and build remarkable experiences. 

We are looking for curious, ambitious makers who want to help define world-class creativity in this new era. We believe the craft is more essential than ever while AI should help people create more, explore more, and unlock new possibilities while keeping creators at the center of the creative process.   

Adobe is amplifying human ingenuity with AI. 

Our Team 

Adobe Creative is Adobe’s in-house brand-creative engine, developing the ideas, campaigns, and assets that power Adobe’s brand and business. We are part of the broader Content & Creative (“C&C”) organization. We work alongside Adobe Content, which focuses on publishing and audience development through owned, earned, and partner channels; an Experiences team, which oversees Adobe’s real-world moments; and shared service teams spanning Video, Talent, Partnerships, and Production.  

Together, C&C commissions and produces work while equipping teams across Adobe’s Global Marketing Organization and the company to create, adapt, and distribute high-quality work with greater speed and consistency. 

The Opportunity  

Adobe makes the tools the world uses to create. Our own design work should set the standard for what those tools make possible. Adobe Creative is looking for an exceptional Senior Multidisciplinary Designer to create beautifully crafted, culturally relevant work across Adobe Creative’s output. 

  

You will work across campaigns, multi-platform design, product storytelling, motion and live experiences, moving confidently between early visual exploration, design development and polished final execution. 

  

Working alongside Design leaders, Creative Directors, Art Directors, Copywriters, Strategists and Product partners, you will help turn ideas into distinctive visual expressions that feel recognizably Adobe without becoming repetitive or formulaic. 

  

You will combine exceptional design craft with curiosity for emerging technology. You will use Creative Cloud, Firefly and AI-enabled workflows to explore more widely, prototype more quickly and make stronger work without compromising taste, originality or human judgment. 

  

You are a maker first. You care deeply about typography, image-making, composition, and the details that make an idea feel fully resolved. 

 

 

What You’ll Do 

Design Across the Work 

  • Create high-quality design across campaigns, multi-platform design, product storytelling, and live experiences.  

  • Develop work from early concept and visual exploration through design development and final execution.  

  • Apply exceptional craft across typography, image-making, layout, composition and art direction.  

  • Work across high-velocity everyday output and highly crafted flagship work.  

  • Adapt strong ideas across channels and formats without losing their intelligence or visual impact. 

  • Create work that feels connected and recognizably Adobe while remaining fresh, distinctive and culturally relevant. 

 

Turn Ideas into Visual Worlds 

  • Partner with Creative Directors, Design Directors and Art Directors to develop visual territories and creative systems.  

  • Translate campaign and creative ideas into compelling art direction and design expression.  

  • Collaborate with Copywriters to develop visual and verbal ideas as one connected creative system.  

  • Create mood boards, prototypes, and design studies that help teams explore and align early.  

  • Know when to explore broadly and when to refine toward a clear, production-ready solution.  

  • Bring a strong visual point of view while remaining open to collaboration and critique. 

 

Build Scalable Creative Systems 

  • Create modular frameworks, templates and reusable design tools that support speed without losing craft.  

  • Help translate Adobe’s brand system into distinctive creative expression across real work.  

  • Test how design ideas perform across channels, formats and audience needs.  

  • Find opportunities to improve tools and workflows based on real creative applications.  

  • Balance systematic thinking with experimentation, surprise and flexibility.  

  • Document design thinking clearly so others can apply it effectively. 

 

Advance AI-Native Design 

  • Use Creative Cloud, Firefly and emerging generative tools throughout concepting, prototyping and production.  

  • Use AI-enabled workflows to expand visual exploration and accelerate iteration without lowering the standard.  

  • Apply human judgment, taste and craft to all AI-assisted work.  

  • Help define where AI can support scale and where human authorship and intervention remain essential.  

  • Test emerging Adobe capabilities through real creative work and share useful feedback with Product teams.  

  • Apply responsible AI practices, including provenance, creator rights and Content Credentials. 

 

Collaborate and Deliver 

  • Work closely with Creative Directors, Art Directors, Copywriters, Motion Designers, Strategists, Producers, Product and Product Marketing.  

  • Present work clearly, explain design decisions, and respond constructively to feedback.  

  • Partner with Production to carry ideas into execution while protecting their creative intent.  

  • Collaborate with photographers, illustrators, artists, studios, and specialist partners when required. 

  • Maintain a high design standard through fast timelines, multiple workstreams, and changing priorities.  

  • Take ownership of your work while contributing generously to the ideas and development of the wider team. 

 

 

What You Need to Succeed 

  • You consider yourself a maker first. AI fluency is how you work, not a skill you are developing. 

  • 6+ years of experience in design, art direction, or multidisciplinary creative practice. 

  • A standout portfolio demonstrating exceptional design craft across multi-platform campaigns and product storytelling. 

  • Deep expertise in typography, layout, image-making, and visual composition. 

  • Strong fluency across digital, motion, and emerging design practices. 

  • Strong conceptual thinking and the ability to carry an idea from exploration through final execution. 

  • Experience working across both high-velocity creative and highly crafted flagship work. 

  • Experience applying brand systems in ways that feel distinctive and alive. 

  • Strong systems thinking and experience creating modular frameworks, templates or reusable creative tools. 

  • Fluency with Adobe Creative Cloud, Firefly and AI-enabled visual workflows. 

  • A clear perspective on how generative AI changes visual exploration, authorship and production.

description:
The Payments & Commercial Abuse Analyst identifies, investigates, and mitigates fraud, abuse, and monetization risks across Adobe's commerce ecosystem. Through data-driven investigations, payment risk analysis, abuse detection, and cross-functional partnerships, the team uncovers emerging threats, develops scalable mitigations, and delivers actionable intelligence that protects revenue, reduces customer friction, and strengthens trust in Adobe products and services. Key Responsibilities & Areas of Impact - The responsibilities below represent the primary areas of focus for this role and may evolve alongside emerging risks, business priorities, and organizational needs. Payments Risk & Commercial Abuse Investigations Investigate complex payment fraud, monetization abuse, account misuse, and commercial abuse schemes impacting Adobe's commerce ecosystem , including unauthorized resale activity, synthetic identity abuse, payment instrument abuse, chargeback fraud, refund abuse, and the unauthorized use, distribution, or commercialization of Adobe products and services. Analyze transactions, customer behaviors, payment activity, subscription usage, account relationships, and associated signals to identify suspicious patterns, assess risk exposure, determine root cause, and recommend mitigation, enforcement, or policy actions. Evaluate escalations, emerging threat patterns, and high-risk activity to develop risk assessments and response recommendations. Analytics, Intelligence & Detection Development Utilize SQL, analytical tools, and investigative methodologies to identify trends, uncover fraud patterns, validate hypotheses, and generate actionable intelligence. Translate investigative findings into scalable detection strategies, risk signals, decisioning logic, and operational controls that reduce fraud while minimizing friction for legitimate customers. Partner with Data Science, Engineering, and AI teams to define abuse indicators, improve model performance, and enhance detection capabilities through investigator-driven insights and feedback loops. Produce intelligence assessments, trend analyses, and strategic insights on emerging abuse patterns, monetization risks, and evolving fraud trends across Adobe's commerce ecosystem. Commerce Risk Strategy & Optimization Balance fraud prevention objectives with customer experience considerations when evaluating controls, policies, detection strategies, and enforcement actions. Provide recommendations to strengthen payment risk controls, fraud mitigation strategies, automation opportunities, and long-term commerce risk initiatives while balancing customer experience and business objectives. Collaborate with Product, Commerce, Risk, Customer Support, Trust & Safety, and Engineering teams to address emerging threats, improve platform resilience, and drive sustainable risk reduction strategies. Qualifications & Core Competencies : Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex investigative findings, payment risk data, and abuse trends into clear, actionable recommendations. Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to identify patterns, assess risk, and transform complex data into meaningful insights that drive informed decision-making. Experience using SQL /SPL and data analysis techniques to support investigations, validate hypotheses, identify trends, and generate actionable intelligence. A naturally inquisitive and investigative mindset, with a passion for understanding how malicious actors exploit commerce systems, products, and business processes. Strong understanding of payment and commerce risk concepts, including chargebacks, friendly fraud, account abuse, refund abuse, affiliate abuse, subscription fraud, identity risk, monetization abuse, and common payment ecosystem risks. Experience identifying risk signals, anomalous behaviors, and abuse patterns and translating findings into scalable detection, mitigation, or enforcement strategies. Creative and strategic problem-solving capabilities, including the ability to anticipate emerging risks and develop innovative, scalable solutions. Proven ability to manage competing priorities and adapt quickly in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. Self-motivated, proactive, and comfortable operating with ambiguity while working independently and collaboratively across cross-functional teams. Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and commitment to delivering thorough, accurate, and high-confidence investigative outcomes. Experience in payments risk, commerce fraud, fraud investigations, abuse prevention, trust and safety operations, fraud analytics, cybersecurity investigations, threat intelligence, or enterprise risk management is preferred. Familiarity with machine learning concepts, risk models, AI-driven abuse trends, or the application of AI and automation to fraud detection and investigative workflows is a plus. Ability to balance fraud prevention objectives with customer experience, operational efficiency, and business outcomes when evaluating risk mitigation strategies. description:
About the role Adobe’s Security Data Platform team builds and operates a petabyte-scale security data lakehouse that turns enterprise telemetry into trusted data for threat detection, investigations, compliance, and security analytics. As a Staff Security Data Engineer, you will own full-system designs and lead critical engineering initiatives across ingestion, storage, governance, orchestration, and data serving. This is a hands-on individual contributor role: you will write and review production code, build infrastructure, define test strategy, fix complex failures, and work with other engineers to deliver the architecture you help shape. You will partner with Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, Compliance, Security Engineering, and infrastructure teams to resolve technical tradeoffs and deliver reliable, cost-effective platform capabilities. Your impact will come through engineering delivery, sound architectural decisions, and helping others become stronger technical leaders. Help us evolve our team from petabyte scale toward exabyte scale! Core responsibilities Platform architecture and engineering Own end-to-end designs that shape the Security Data Platform’s fundamental architecture on Databricks and AWS, using Spark, Delta Lake, and Unity Catalog. Translate ambiguous needs into design proposals, implementation plans, and production capabilities. Build and evolve distributed batch and streaming pipelines for EDR telemetry, network logs, identity events, cloud audit logs, and new security data sources. Design for throughput, fault tolerance, replay, schema evolution, and sub-minute freshness where use cases require it. Write maintainable Python and SQL, develop complex platform features, and refactor unreliable code. Establish reusable engineering patterns, lead code and design reviews, and own test strategy and automation choices across pipelines and infrastructure. Build and maintain tested, reusable Terraform modules for AWS and Databricks infrastructure, including S3, IAM, VPC networking, and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA). Automate delivery through version control and CI/CD. Data modeling governance and operations Design layered lakehouse data models and reusable normalization patterns, including Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) mappings where appropriate. Preserve source fidelity and make datasets useful for investigations, analytics, and detection workloads. Establish data contracts, quality checks, cataloging, classification, lineage, access controls, and retention policies with data owners. Use Unity Catalog to make data ownership and governance traceable from raw events to analyst-facing datasets. Engineer and operate Airflow and MWAA orchestration, including dependencies, retries, backfills, alerting, and automated recovery. Define service level objectives with consumers and instrument data freshness, completeness, pipeline health, and query performance. Lead diagnosis and resolution of complex production issues across Spark, storage, orchestration, and cloud infrastructure. Improve incident response, runbooks, recovery testing, and operational readiness to prevent recurring failures. Performance and technical leadership Profile workloads and lead measurable cost and performance improvements through query and Spark tuning, storage lifecycle policies, partitioning, and compute right-sizing. Establish baselines and dashboards that show savings alongside reliability, latency, and capacity. Lead cross-team technical discussions, reconcile competing requirements, and build agreement on architecture and delivery priorities without formal management authority. Communicate decisions, landmarks, risks, and business impact proactively to your manager and partners. Partner with detection and security analytics engineers to deliver the data interfaces, governance, and pipeline capabilities needed for SIEM modernization and automated detection deployment. Mentor engineers through pairing, technical reviews, documentation, and knowledge sharing. Help others lead technical work, promote inclusive debate, and contribute to hiring decisions through technical assessment. Evaluate and introduce useful platform innovations, including AI-assisted engineering and operational automation. Validate outputs, protect sensitive security data, measure improvements, and help partner teams adopt proven approaches. Required qualifications Substantial experience building and operating production data platforms, typically 10 or more years in data or software engineering, with demonstrated Staff-level scope and impact. Equivalent depth and outcomes are welcome; a prior Staff or Principal title is not required. A record of personally delivering complex distributed systems and leading full-system design and implementation across team boundaries. Ability to turn general, unstructured assignments into clear technical approaches and working software. Deep production expertise in Spark's traditional and real-time data workloads, Databricks, Delta Lake, and lakehouse architecture; strong Python and advanced SQL skills for data modeling, profiling, and query optimization. Strong AWS experience across storage, compute, networking, and IAM, plus production Terraform experience designing, testing, and maintaining reusable infrastructure modules. Practical understanding of distributed systems, including partitioning, replication, consistency, back pressure, scalability, and fault tolerance, with experience diagnosing failures across system boundaries. Experience with Airflow, MWAA, or equivalent orchestration, and with production observability, data quality, automated testing, CI/CD, and reliable deployment and recovery practices. Demonstrated ability to improve platform cost, performance, and reliability with measurable results; sound judgment in balancing these goals against security and consumer requirements. Effective technical communication and multi-functional influence, including leading design reviews, resolving disagreements, mentoring engineers, and building adoption of shared engineering practices. Preferred qualifications Experience with security telemetry, OCSF or comparable security schemas, and data requirements for SIEM, SOAR, threat detection, or investigations. Experience with Unity Catalog governance, data classification and retention, regional data controls, or multi-region platform design. Experience with Cribl Stream, Vector, or similar telemetry routing and enrichment tools, and platform integrations supporting automated threat detection rollout. About the role

Adobe’s Security Data Platform team builds and operates a petabyte-scale security data lakehouse that turns enterprise telemetry into trusted data for threat detection, investigations, compliance, and security analytics.
 

As a Staff Security Data Engineer, you will own full-system designs and lead critical engineering initiatives across ingestion, storage, governance, orchestration, and data serving. This is a hands-on individual contributor role: you will write and review production code, build infrastructure, define test strategy, fix complex failures, and work with other engineers to deliver the architecture you help shape.
 

You will partner with Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, Compliance, Security Engineering, and infrastructure teams to resolve technical tradeoffs and deliver reliable, cost-effective platform capabilities. Your impact will come through engineering delivery, sound architectural decisions, and helping others become stronger technical leaders.
 

Help us evolve our team from petabyte scale toward exabyte scale!
 

Core responsibilities

Platform architecture and engineering

  • Own end-to-end designs that shape the Security Data Platform’s fundamental architecture on Databricks and AWS, using Spark, Delta Lake, and Unity Catalog. Translate ambiguous needs into design proposals, implementation plans, and production capabilities.
  • Build and evolve distributed batch and streaming pipelines for EDR telemetry, network logs, identity events, cloud audit logs, and new security data sources. Design for throughput, fault tolerance, replay, schema evolution, and sub-minute freshness where use cases require it.
  • Write maintainable Python and SQL, develop complex platform features, and refactor unreliable code. Establish reusable engineering patterns, lead code and design reviews, and own test strategy and automation choices across pipelines and infrastructure.
  • Build and maintain tested, reusable Terraform modules for AWS and Databricks infrastructure, including S3, IAM, VPC networking, and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA). Automate delivery through version control and CI/CD.

Data modeling governance and operations

  • Design layered lakehouse data models and reusable normalization patterns, including Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) mappings where appropriate. Preserve source fidelity and make datasets useful for investigations, analytics, and detection workloads.
  • Establish data contracts, quality checks, cataloging, classification, lineage, access controls, and retention policies with data owners. Use Unity Catalog to make data ownership and governance traceable from raw events to analyst-facing datasets.
  • Engineer and operate Airflow and MWAA orchestration, including dependencies, retries, backfills, alerting, and automated recovery. Define service level objectives with consumers and instrument data freshness, completeness, pipeline health, and query performance.
  • Lead diagnosis and resolution of complex production issues across Spark, storage, orchestration, and cloud infrastructure. Improve incident response, runbooks, recovery testing, and operational readiness to prevent recurring failures.

Performance and technical leadership

  • Profile workloads and lead measurable cost and performance improvements through query and Spark tuning, storage lifecycle policies, partitioning, and compute right-sizing. Establish baselines and dashboards that show savings alongside reliability, latency, and capacity.
  • Lead cross-team technical discussions, reconcile competing requirements, and build agreement on architecture and delivery priorities without formal management authority. Communicate decisions, landmarks, risks, and business impact proactively to your manager and partners.
  • Partner with detection and security analytics engineers to deliver the data interfaces, governance, and pipeline capabilities needed for SIEM modernization and automated detection deployment.
  • Mentor engineers through pairing, technical reviews, documentation, and knowledge sharing. Help others lead technical work, promote inclusive debate, and contribute to hiring decisions through technical assessment.
  • Evaluate and introduce useful platform innovations, including AI-assisted engineering and operational automation. Validate outputs, protect sensitive security data, measure improvements, and help partner teams adopt proven approaches.
     

Required qualifications

  • Substantial experience building and operating production data platforms, typically 10 or more years in data or software engineering, with demonstrated Staff-level scope and impact. Equivalent depth and outcomes are welcome; a prior Staff or Principal title is not required.
  • A record of personally delivering complex distributed systems and leading full-system design and implementation across team boundaries. Ability to turn general, unstructured assignments into clear technical approaches and working software.
  • Deep production expertise in Spark's traditional and real-time data workloads, Databricks, Delta Lake, and lakehouse architecture; strong Python and advanced SQL skills for data modeling, profiling, and query optimization.
  • Strong AWS experience across storage, compute, networking, and IAM, plus production Terraform experience designing, testing, and maintaining reusable infrastructure modules.
  • Practical understanding of distributed systems, including partitioning, replication, consistency, back pressure, scalability, and fault tolerance, with experience diagnosing failures across system boundaries.
  • Experience with Airflow, MWAA, or equivalent orchestration, and with production observability, data quality, automated testing, CI/CD, and reliable deployment and recovery practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to improve platform cost, performance, and reliability with measurable results; sound judgment in balancing these goals against security and consumer requirements.
  • Effective technical communication and multi-functional influence, including leading design reviews, resolving disagreements, mentoring engineers, and building adoption of shared engineering practices.
     

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with security telemetry, OCSF or comparable security schemas, and data requirements for SIEM, SOAR, threat detection, or investigations.
  • Experience with Unity Catalog governance, data classification and retention, regional data controls, or multi-region platform design.
  • Experience with Cribl Stream, Vector, or similar telemetry routing and enrichment tools, and platform integrations supporting automated threat detection rollout.

The Opportunity This position where we will develop and launch a new product within Adobe working within an exciting org that is incubating next-generation ideas. Build the next generation agentic AI platform working with a research scientist, designers, and a venture lead to bring the new product to life. This role is an outstanding opportunity to operate like a startup founding engineer while having the resources of an innovative, large Technology company. Join us for an opportunity to invent new technologies and power a brand-new product that serves emerging creators. The Challenge We are looking for a Founding Full Stack Engineer to build Creator Services from the ground up. Creator Services is building AI-powered audience intelligence: given a content idea and creator context, predict whether it will resonate and surface the insights that help creators make smarter decisions. As Creator Services expands into brand deal discovery, negotiation, storefront management, and affiliate programs, the research agenda grows with it. A core part of the platform will be agentic AI systems that automate the complex tasks creators face running their businesses. You will build and operate multi-agent pipelines. You will transform model outputs into interactive creator workflows. This will connect Creator Services to creator platforms and data sources that make the intelligence real. Collaborate closely with the Research Lead and Product & UX Lead as a peer collaborator. This includes cost-efficient inference, caching, and graceful degradation when model providers falter. Also, include eval instrumentation to catch regressions in production. Model Productionization: Collaborate closely alongside the lead researcher to transform model outputs into responsive, low-latency creator workflows. Support deployment of trainable model components alongside base model APIs (Azure OpenAI) on Colligo (Adobe's ML platform). Integrations: Build integrations with external creator platforms (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok via creator-authorized OAuth), Adobe's wider suite of creative tools (Express, Firefly, Adobe Creative Suite, IMS), Semrush, and internal Adobe services. Data Pipelines: Build the data pipelines that feed the audience intelligence, insight, and prediction engines — including the outcome-feedback loop that lets the system learn from real creator results. Architecture Ownership: Own architecture decisions as an early hire — from framework choices to data models to deployment pipelines Observability & Reliability: Contribute to monitoring, observability, and evaluation frameworks that ensure AI-driven features behave reliably and transparently for creators. What is needed to succeed 5+ years shipping full-stack products end-to-end (front-end + back-end + APIs) — startup or 0→1 experience strongly preferred. Proficiency in a modern back-end environment like Python or Node with TypeScript is required. Experience with a contemporary app/front-end stack such as React, React Native, or Flutter is also necessary. Mobile-first experience is a strong plus. Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs and agent frameworks; solid grasp of latency, cost, evals, and fallbacks in production — not just prototypes. Experience designing and building scalable APIs, backend services, and data pipelines from scratch. Comfort with cloud infra (Azure/AWS/GCP) and standing up services in a resource-constrained startup environment. Ability to move fast under ambiguity, own outcomes end-to-end, and work effectively in a small, flat team. A genuine interest in the creator economy and the tools creators use to build their businesses. Bonus Experience with third-party social/platform APIs (YouTube Data API, Instagram Graph API, TikTok for Developers). Familiarity with the Adobe ecosystem — Firefly APIs, Adobe IMS, Creative Cloud integrations. Experience with recommender or ML-serving systems; Colligo or similar ML infrastructure. description:
The CSC Business Consultant leads customers through business transformation as they adopt Adobe’s Content Supply Chain solutions . You will help customers improve how content is planned, created, managed, and delivered by defining business requirements, future-state workflows, operating models, and adoption strategies. This role combines strong business consulting with hands-on solution delivery. You will connect business goals to platform capabilities, configure solutions, and build and validate workflows and integrations across Workfront, AEM Assets, and connected CSC tools. You will independently deliver standard configurations and moderately complex automations, partnering with Technical Consultants and architects on advanced integrations, custom development, security, and solution architecture. What You Will Do Customer Strategy and Process Design Lead discovery workshops to understand current processes, pain points, stakeholder needs, and business priorities across the content lifecycle. Use industry knowledge and CSC experience to recommend future-state workflows, operating models, and implementation priorities. Translate customer goals into business requirements, process maps, user stories, and acceptance criteria; partner with technical teams to confirm feasibility and implementation alignment. Content Strategy and Governance Define organizational taxonomy, metadata standards, asset lifecycle rules, and governance aligned with customer needs and relevant industry practices. Design intake processes, roles and responsibilities, approval paths, and asset management use cases spanning Workfront and AEM Assets. Define how metadata moves between systems, document field mappings and ownership, and validate that configurations support the intended business process. Change Management and Adoption Assess organizational readiness and support stakeholder alignment, communication planning, and adoption strategies. Create and deliver role-based training, playbooks, standard operating procedures, and process documentation. Lead business UAT planning and customer walkthroughs, validate results against acceptance criteria, and support knowledge transfer and post-go-live self-sufficiency. Practical Solution Delivery Independently configure and test forms, templates, approval workflows, reports, metadata structures, and permissions within agreed solution standards. Build and maintain moderately complex Fusion workflows using branching, field mappings, data transformations, API calls, and error handling; validate connected processes end to end. Troubleshoot configuration and integration issues using execution logs, API responses, and data validation; resolve issues within scope and escalate architectural or code-level problems with clear findings. Program Execution and Value Realization Manage scope, risks, dependencies, and decisions with Project Managers and Engagement Leads; communicate roadblocks and tradeoffs early. Establish baseline measures and KPIs with customers, track business outcomes, and deliver executive readouts on progress, adoption, and value. Support sales and scoping discussions by clarifying business needs, expected outcomes, delivery assumptions, and implementation considerations. Required Skills and Experience 7+ years in business consulting, business analysis, marketing operations, or related transformation roles. Strong understanding of marketing workflows, content production lifecycles, and enterprise content or asset management. Strong working knowledge of Adobe’s Content Supply Chain ecosystem, including Workfront, AEM Assets, and Fusion, with hands-on implementation experience in at least one core platform. Ability to turn ambiguous needs into structured workflows, requirements, acceptance criteria, and practical platform recommendations. Practical experience with REST APIs, JSON, field mappings, and data transformations; able to inspect requests and responses, work with established authentication methods, and test system-to-system data flows. Hands-on experience building and troubleshooting multi-step automations in Fusion or a comparable integration platform, including conditional logic and error handling; able to deliver independently within defined architecture and security standards. Strong facilitation, presentation, documentation, and executive communication skills; experience navigating organizational change and stakeholder alignment. Willingness to travel up to 50%. Preferred Experience Experience delivering production Workfront Fusion integrations and supporting monitoring, recovery, and ongoing maintenance. Experience implementing metadata or taxonomy standards across connected platforms, or working with Frame.io and other CSC tools. Experience using AI-powered tools to support discovery, documentation, workflow analysis, or delivery efficiency. Success Looks Like Customers have a clear future-state operating model and adopt workflows tied to measurable business outcomes. Business requirements translate into well-tested configurations and maintainable integrations, with clear documentation and reliable handoffs between systems and teams. Stakeholders understand their roles and next steps, and can sustain the solution after go-live. The Opportunity 


We're looking for an attorney to join Adobe's Ethics and Compliance Office, working to ensure Adobe acts with integrity across its business. The role will have a strong focus on trade compliance and will also stretch across other compliance matters, including anti-bribery and corruption. This role is part of a collaborative and tight-knit team, reporting to Adobe's Director of Trade Compliance within the Ethics and Compliance Office. You'll work with business and legal teams across Adobe to deliver business-centric advice and develop practical solutions that use technology to drive compliance.


What you'll Do 

  • Advise Adobe product teams on global trade regulations, including sanctions, export controls, customs, and supply chain rules.
  • Provide day-to-day trade and anticorruption compliance guidance and track emerging regulatory trends
  • Advise Adobe's restricted party screening function on controls, processes, and procedures, including supporting and developing automation.
  • Provide strategic trade and anticorruption compliance advice for complex commercial agreements, including drafting and negotiating terms.
  • Maintain strong relationships across the business to effectively spot and address trade and antibribery/anticorruption compliance risks.
  • Support trade and anticorruption compliance activities related to merger-and-acquisition due diligence and business-integration activities.
  • Provide training on trade compliance topics to cross-functional teams, including sales, product, engineering, and legal colleagues.
  • Handle regulatory inquiries and filings with U.S. and other agencies, as needed.
  • Advise on other compliance matters.

What you need to succeed 

  • Law degree/JD, with a mix of law firm and in-house experience preferred;
  • 5+ years of legal experience advising on U.S. economic sanctions and export control laws and other compliance regulations;
  • Experience advising multinational companies (preferably in the tech sector) on non-U.S. trade laws, including EU and UK sanctions and export control regimes;
  • Passion for developing and using technology in legal practice;
  • Highly effective communicator who can translate complex regulations into actionable guidance for business and compliance teams;
  • A self-starter who can operate independently in a dynamic global environment;
  • An approachable and flexible manner with a great sense of humor; and
  • Willingness to work flexible hours (this role requires frequent collaboration with non-US-based team members).
